title: nail supports HMMER's gathering, trusted and noise cutoffs
body:
HMMER profiles from Pfam and similar libraries carry curated score thresholds in their header. Each of the `GA`, `TC` and `NC` lines holds two bit scores. `hmmsearch` and `hmmscan` use them through `--cut_ga`, `--cut_tc` and `--cut_nc` in place of the E-value thresholds.

```text
GA    25.00 25.00;
TC    25.10 25.40;
NC    24.90 24.70;
```

nail ignores these lines today. The header parser in `libnail/src/structs/p7hmm.rs` matches `NAME`, `ACC`, `LENG`, `ALPH`, `STATS` and `HMM`, and drops every other keyword. The one reporting filter is `-E` (`PipelineArgs::e_value_threshold`, default 10), applied in `OutputStage` in `nail/src/pipeline/output_stage.rs`.

## Proposal

- parse `GA`, `TC` and `NC` into the profile
- add CLI flags that report a hit only when its score clears the chosen cutoff, with the same names HMMER uses
- print a warning line in red whenever a cutoff flag is set, saying that HMMER trained these cutoffs on its own scores and that nail's scores may not line up with them

The work starts by reading the HMMER source (`p7_pipeline.c` and the model header parsing) to pin down what the flags do. The behaviour to match includes these cases:

- what the flags do to the reporting threshold and to the inclusion threshold
- whether the flags replace `-E`, `-T`, `--domE` and `--domT`, or sit beside them
- what HMMER does when a model lacks the requested line
- whether `--cut_*` changes `Z` or `domZ`

## Open

Are the cutoffs sequence scores or domain scores? From memory of the HMMER user guide, the first value on each line is a per-sequence bit score and the second is a per-domain bit score, and `--cut_ga` applies both. Nobody has checked that against the source yet. If it holds, nail has to decide what its score corresponds to. A nail hit is scored by Forward over the region the cloud search bounds, so it is neither HMMER's whole-sequence score nor a domain score from domain definition. Which of the two values nail compares against is undecided.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/87ab289b
notes.text:
How HMMER 3.4 uses the cutoffs, read from the source in `hmmer-3.4/src`. Lines marked checked were read directly; the rest come from a sub-agent's read and are cited for checking.

## Parsing

- `p7_hmmfile.c:1428` (checked): a protein `GA`, `TC` or `NC` line needs two values, and a missing one is a format error. A DNA or RNA line needs one, and the second is copied from it. `atof` reads each value, so a non-number becomes 0.0 without an error. Extra tokens are ignored.
- value 1 goes to `cutoff[p7_GA1]`, the per-sequence cutoff, and value 2 to `cutoff[p7_GA2]`, the per-domain cutoff (`hmmer.h:73`)
- unset cutoffs hold `p7_CUTOFF_UNSET`, -99999.0

## Flags

- `hmmsearch.c:50` (checked): each `--cut_*` flag is incompatible with `-E`, `-T`, `--domE`, `--domT`, `--incE`, `--incT`, `--incdomE`, `--incdomT` and the other two `--cut_*` flags
- `p7_pipeline_Create`, `p7_pipeline.c:168` (checked): the flag switches reporting and inclusion, for sequences and for domains, from E-values to bit scores
- `p7_pli_NewModelThresholds`, `p7_pipeline.c:538` (checked), runs once per query model: `T = incT = GA1` and `domT = incdomT = GA2`

## Comparison

- `p7_pli_TargetReportable`, `p7_pipeline.c:414` (checked): a sequence passes when `score >= T`
- the sequence score is the bias-corrected whole-sequence bit score, or the sum of domain scores when that is larger (`p7_pipeline.c` near 832)
- a domain passes when `dcl[d].bitscore >= domT`
- the domain thresholds never decide whether a sequence is reported. A sequence above value 1 with no domain above value 2 is still reported, with "No individual domains that satisfy reporting thresholds" (`p7_tophits.c:1315`).

## Missing cutoff

`p7_pipeline.c:543` (checked) fails with "GA bit thresholds unavailable on model %s". hmmsearch then calls `p7_Fail` and the whole run exits (`hmmsearch.c:503`). Only value 1 is tested for being unset.

## Unchanged by the flags

- `Z`, `domZ` and E-values are computed as usual and still printed
- the F1, F2 and F3 filter P-value thresholds keep their values, so a hit above the cutoff can still be dropped by a filter
- the output header gains `# model-specific thresholding:     GA cutoffs` (`hmmsearch.c:243`)

## Answer to the open question

HMMER uses both values. Value 1, the sequence cutoff, alone decides whether a hit is reported. Value 2 decides only which domains of a reported hit are shown.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/87ab289b
notes.text:
Jack decided three points of the design.

- The flags follow nail's kebab-case convention: `--cut-ga`, `--cut-tc`, `--cut-nc`. HMMER's underscore spellings are not accepted.
- nail checks for the requested cutoff on every profile when it loads them, and fails before seeding when one lacks it. HMMER instead fails when it reaches that model.
- nail compares against value 2, the per-domain cutoff. A nail score is the Forward score of one alignment over one cloud region. That makes it far closer to HMMER's best-domain score than to HMMER's whole-sequence score.

One consequence follows from the HMMER notes above. HMMER reports a hit whose sequence score clears value 1 even when no domain clears value 2, and nail does not. Where value 1 and value 2 are equal, as in most Pfam models, the two differ only by the gap between a sequence score and its best domain score.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/87ab289b
notes.text: The libnail side landed in `b85ef4b`. `Profile` has `gathering`, `trusted` and `noise`, each an `Option<Cutoff>` with `sequence` and `domain` in `Bits`, parsed by `Profile::from_p7hmm` and carried by `Profile::serialize`.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/87ab289b
notes.text:
An end-to-end check of `--cut-ga` on the fixtures, `fixtures/query.hmm` against `fixtures/target.fa` at 4 threads, compared with `hmmsearch --cut_ga` (HMMER 3.4).

- `--cut-ga` reported 396 hits, and every one scores at least its profile's GA domain value
- each of the 12 hits that `-E 10` reports and `--cut-ga` drops scores below that value
- nail reports no hit that `hmmsearch --cut_ga` lacks

`hmmsearch` reports four 7tm_1 hits that nail misses, with or without the flag. The four targets are D4AC13, E5DHB5, E7FE13 and F1MLX5, all Leucine-rich repeat-containing receptors. Their best domain scores run from 48.5 to 60.1 bits. mmseqs wrote no seed for any of the four pairs, and 7tm_1 had 107 seeds, under the `--max-seqs` limit. The miss happens in seeding, before the cutoff runs, and nobody has traced it further.
